text.p: These are the leading stories in the Namibian press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Former Rossing Uranium engineer and cancer victim, Edward Connelly, on Thursday finally won his long legal battle to have the right to bring his compensation case in the British courts. Britain's house of Lords granted him the right to use British legal aid to continue his N$3 million claim in London against the British mining multinational Rio Tinto Plc, which owns Rossing.
- Illegal skin lightening creams worth around N$40,000 have been seized from traders in Oshakati's open market and were burnt by health officials.
- The Angolan defence ministry has described the situation in Angola as critical, following a mobilisation of Unita rebels on the north-eastern border and the Cabinda enclave.

- Minister of lands Pendukeni Ithana has told farmers, who offer land for sale to the government, to ensure that they do not offer merely a fragment of a farm, but a whole entity, registered as such with the ministry of agriculture.
- Horror stories of sodomy and intimidation in police cells, as well as bribery of police officers are being reported to lawyers from prisons all over the country.
- Age old camelthorn trees near Rehoboth are being destroyed by vandals.
